overall_diagnosis: The produced workbook appears incomplete or not properly constructed as an Excel model: required source data ranges, projection/extension formulas, and cross-sheet links were missing across multiple sheets. The verifier failures consistently point to absent or non-preserved formulas (rather than incorrect economics), suggesting weaknesses in end-to-end spreadsheet population, formula authoring, reference linking, and post-save validation/recalculation.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The agent failed to populate and/or preserve the Excel workbook’s required data and formulas. Reported missing elements include populated PWT/CFC data, WEO projection formulas, the depreciation formula in Production!B3, LN/EXP/TREND/AVERAGE formula families used for extensions/filters, and references from the Investment sheet. This indicates insufficient enforcement of: (1) writing formulas into the specified cells/ranges (not leaving blanks or hardcoding), (2) maintaining cross-sheet references, and (3) validating that formulas persist and recalculate after saving.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Augment the xlsx workflow with an explicit end-to-end build-and-verify checklist for multi-sheet economic/financial models: (1) Populate all required source tables/ranges (e.g., PWT/WEO) and confirm non-empty coverage across the expected years/countries; (2) Implement projections/extensions using formulas (not pasted values), specifically ensuring required formula families are present where instructed (LN, EXP, TREND, AVERAGE, ratio/division calculations, depreciation/capital accumulation); (3) Ensure cross-sheet links are created and intact (e.g., Investment -> Production/WEO_Data), using consistent absolute/relative references and fill-down/right across required ranges; (4) Recalculate the workbook, scan for any formula errors (#REF!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #NAME?, #N/A), and confirm key sentinel cells like Production!B3 contain formulas; (5) After saving/exporting, re-open and re-check that formulas and links persisted and that expected ranges still contain formulas (not blanks).
